title: Coinneach follows his brother north
summary: Coinneach mac Shuibhne, unable to wait out a year of silence, sets off after his brother with a sack of oatcake and a skin of buttermilk, following the roads he judges Ailean must have taken toward the grove of Doire ghlas.

title: The camp beyond the oaks
summary: Coinneach comes within sight of the seven fires at Doire ghlas and finds he cannot cross into the ring of oaks. The Keeper allows him to camp at the tree-line and no nearer, and he keeps his own vigil there through the seven nights of his brother's watch.

title: Voices heard on the fifth night
summary: On the fifth night of the vigil Coinneach hears, low under the sound of the fires, what he takes for voices, one of them shaped almost like his brother's speech though fallen into a rhythm Ailean never used. He never swears to more than that he heard something.

title: The grove fills with light
summary: On the eighth night, when the seven fires go dark together, Coinneach watches the grove of Doire ghlas fill with a light that is not firelight, and sees shapes moving among the oaks. His feet will not carry him past the tree-line to follow them.

title: The six pots left cold
summary: At dawn the six pots that carried Ailean's fires north are found lying empty on the leaves of Doire ghlas, their turf lids scattered, and the pale stone that held the seventh coal lies among them, giving no light but warm to the touch.

title: Coinneach finds his brother warm at dawn
summary: Ailean walks out of the grove at morning and catches his stumbling brother by the arm. Coinneach feels a warmth in it like a hearthstone long after the fire is swept, and knows before any word is said that the night has changed his brother.

title: "They named me king"
summary: Ailean tells his brother only this much of the night in the grove: that he has been named king. He says nothing of who named him, of what a king might be king of, or of what was put into him, and Coinneach asks no further, having seen enough from outside the trees.

title: The brothers turn south
summary: Ailean gathers the six empty pots onto his shoulder-pole, leaves the pale seventh stone lying uncovered among the leaves of Doire ghlas, and sets out south with his brother, never lighting the six fires again.

title: Ailean passes Na Glinn Àrda
summary: Ailean walks south past the households of Clann na Ceiste in Na Glinn Àrda without turning aside to any hearth, though he has kin enough among them to be fed and questioned there.

title: Eleven kin walk south with him
summary: Households of Clann na Ceiste near Na Glinn Àrda leave byre and field to follow Ailean south, eleven in all, none able afterward to give a better reason than a feeling not to be argued with. The king shares out Coinneach's sack among them on the road.

title: The bare ring in the frost
summary: Twice on the road south the company sleeps in the open, and both mornings the frost that silvers the field leaves a bare, warm ring the size of a sleeping man where Ailean lay, as it did at his feet in the grove.

title: Coinneach keeps the first telling
summary: Walking south behind his brother, Coinneach turns over what little he saw from outside the ring of oaks and fits it into an account he is careful never to swell beyond what he truly witnessed, the seed of the telling Clann na Ceiste keep of the seven nights.
